audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for purity/tradition debate, Isaiah citation, Corban, heart-output teaching, Syrophoenician woman, and deaf man healing with Ephphatha.

verses.restored: The Pharisees and some of the scribes gathered to him, having come from Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.

modern.text: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus,

original.text: Καὶ συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων

verses.restored: They saw some of his disciples eating bread with common/unclean hands, that is, unwashed.

familiar.text: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.

modern.text: and they saw some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled—that is, unwashed.

original.text: καὶ ἰδόντες τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ⸂ὅτι κοιναῖς χερσίν, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις, ἐσθίουσιν⸃ ⸀τοὺς ⸀ἄρτους—

verses.restored: For the Pharisees and all the Judeans do not eat unless they wash their hands with the fist, holding the tradition of the elders.

familiar.text: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.

modern.text: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.

original.text: οἱ γὰρ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐὰν μὴ πυγμῇ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων,

verses.restored: When they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash; and there are many other things they received to hold: washings of cups, pitchers, and vessels.

familiar.text: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.

modern.text: And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.

original.text: καὶ ἀπʼ ⸀ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ ⸀βαπτίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν, βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων ⸂καὶ κλινῶν⸃—

verses.restored: The Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with common/unclean hands?

familiar.text: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?

modern.text: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.”

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς· Διὰ τί ⸂οὐ περιπατοῦσιν οἱ μαθηταί σου⸃ κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀλλὰ ⸀κοιναῖς χερσὶν ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον;

verses.restored: He said to them, Isaiah prophesied beautifully about you hypocrites, as it has been written: This people honors me with lips, but their heart is far away from me.

familiar.text: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

modern.text: Jesus answered them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.

original.text: ὁ ⸀δὲ εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν Ἠσαΐας περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν, ὡς γέγραπται ⸀ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ·

verses.restored: In vain they worship me, teaching as teachings the commands of humans.

familiar.text: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

modern.text: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’

original.text: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων·

verses.restored: Leaving the command of the Divine, you hold the tradition of humans.

familiar.text: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.

modern.text: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men. ”

original.text: ⸀ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ κρατεῖτε τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ⸀ἀνθρώπων.

verses.restored: He said to them, Beautifully do you set aside the command of the Divine so that you may keep your tradition.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.

modern.text: He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.

original.text: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Καλῶς ἀθετεῖτε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν ⸀τηρήσητε·

verses.restored: For Moses said, Honor your father and your mother, and, The one speaking evil of father or mother must surely come to an end.

familiar.text: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:

modern.text: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’

original.text: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ εἶπεν· Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου, καί· Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω·

verses.restored: But you say, If a person says to father or mother, Whatever you might have gained from me is Corban, that is, gift-offering,

familiar.text: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.

modern.text: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift devoted to God),

original.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε· Ἐὰν εἴπῃ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί· Κορβᾶν, ὅ ἐστιν Δῶρον, ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς,

verses.restored: then you no longer allow him to do anything for father or mother,

familiar.text: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;

modern.text: he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.

original.text: ⸀οὐκέτι ἀφίετε αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ποιῆσαι τῷ ⸀πατρὶ ἢ τῇ ⸀μητρί,

verses.restored: making void the word of the Divine by your tradition that you handed down; and many such things you do.

familiar.text: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.

modern.text: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.” What Defiles a Man (Matthew 15:10–20)

original.text: ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ παραδόσει ὑμῶν ᾗ παρεδώκατε· καὶ παρόμοια τοιαῦτα πολλὰ ποιεῖτε.

verses.restored: Calling the crowd again, he said to them, Hear me, all of you, and understand.

familiar.text: And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:

modern.text: Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:

original.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ⸀πάλιν τὸν ὄχλον ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· ⸀Ἀκούσατέ μου πάντες καὶ ⸀σύνετε.

verses.restored: There is nothing outside a person that, entering into him, is able to make him common/unclean; but the things coming out of a person are what make the person common/unclean.

familiar.text: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.

modern.text: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.”

original.text: οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς αὐτὸν ὃ δύναται ⸂κοινῶσαι αὐτόν⸃· ἀλλὰ τὰ ⸂ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενά⸃ ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ⸀ἄνθρωπον.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.]

familiar.text: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

modern.note: The BSB follows modern critical-text practice here and does not print this traditional verse number as a separate verse.

original.note: This traditional verse number is not present as a separate verse in the SBLGNT base text; preserve as a textual-witness issue.

verses.restored: When he entered a house away from the crowd, his disciples asked him about the parable.

familiar.text: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.

modern.text: After Jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, His disciples inquired about the parable.

original.text: Καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθεν ⸀εἰς οἶκον ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου, ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸂τὴν παραβολήν⸃.

verses.restored: He said to them, Are you also without understanding? Do you not perceive that everything outside entering a person is not able to make him common/unclean,

familiar.text: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;

modern.text: “Are you still so dull?” He asked. “Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε; οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἔξωθεν εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὐ δύναται αὐτὸν κοινῶσαι,

verses.restored: because it does not enter his heart but his belly, and goes out into the latrine, cleansing all foods.

familiar.text: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?

modern.text: because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.” (Thus all foods are clean.)

original.text: ὅτι οὐκ εἰσπορεύεται αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἀλλʼ εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν, καὶ εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκπορεύεται;— ⸀καθαρίζων πάντα τὰ βρώματα.

verses.restored: He said, What comes out of a person, that makes the person common/unclean.

familiar.text: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.

modern.text: He continued: “What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.

original.text: ἔλεγεν δὲ ὅτι Τὸ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκεῖνο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον·

verses.restored: For from within, out of the heart of humans, come harmful reasonings, sexual immoralities, thefts, murders, adulteries,

familiar.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

modern.text: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,

original.text: ἔσωθεν γὰρ ἐκ τῆς καρδίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ διαλογισμοὶ οἱ κακοὶ ἐκπορεύονται, ⸂πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, φόνοι,

verses.restored: greed, harmful acts, deceit, sensual excess, a harmful eye, slander, pride, foolishness.

familiar.text: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:

modern.text: greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.

original.text: μοιχεῖαι⸃, πλεονεξίαι, πονηρίαι, δόλος, ἀσέλγεια, ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός, βλασφημία, ὑπερηφανία, ἀφροσύνη·

verses.restored: All these harmful things come out from within and make a person common/unclean.

familiar.text: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.

modern.text: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.” The Faith of the Gentile Woman (Matthew 15:21–28)

original.text: πάντα ταῦτα τὰ πονηρὰ ἔσωθεν ἐκπορεύεται καὶ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

verses.restored: From there he rose and went away into the borders of Tyre. Entering a house, he wanted no one to know, yet he could not be hidden.

familiar.text: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.

modern.text: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre. Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice.

original.text: ⸂Ἐκεῖθεν δὲ⸃ ἀναστὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὰ ⸀ὅρια ⸀Τύρου. καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς οἰκίαν οὐδένα ἤθελεν γνῶναι, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθη λαθεῖν·

verses.restored: Immediately, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him and came and fell at his feet.

familiar.text: For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:

modern.text: Instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.

original.text: ⸂ἀλλʼ εὐθὺς ἀκούσασα⸃ γυνὴ περὶ αὐτοῦ, ἧς εἶχεν τὸ θυγάτριον αὐτῆς πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον, ἐλθοῦσα προσέπεσεν πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: The woman was Greek, Syrophoenician by birth. She asked him to cast the unclean spirit out of her daughter.

familiar.text: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.

modern.text: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.

original.text: ⸂ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἦν⸃ Ἑλληνίς, Συροφοινίκισσα τῷ γένει· καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτὸν ἵνα τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐκβάλῃ ἐκ τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: He said to her, Let the children be filled first, for it is not beautiful/good to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs.

familiar.text: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.

modern.text: “First let the children have their fill,” He said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἔλεγεν⸃ αὐτῇ· Ἄφες πρῶτον χορτασθῆναι τὰ τέκνα, οὐ γὰρ ⸂καλόν ἐστιν⸃ λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ ⸂τοῖς κυναρίοις βαλεῖν⸃.

verses.restored: She answered him, Lord, even the little dogs under the table eat from the children's crumbs.

familiar.text: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.

modern.text: “Yes, Lord,” she replied, “even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

original.text: ἡ δὲ ἀπεκρίθη καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· ⸀Κύριε, ⸀καὶ τὰ κυνάρια ὑποκάτω τῆς τραπέζης ⸀ἐσθίουσιν ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν παιδίων.

verses.restored: He said to her, Because of this word, go; the unclean spirit has gone out from your daughter.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.

modern.text: Then Jesus told her, “Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Διὰ τοῦτον τὸν λόγον ὕπαγε, ἐξελήλυθεν ⸂ἐκ τῆς θυγατρός σου τὸ δαιμόνιον⸃.

verses.restored: Going away to her house, she found the child lying on the bed and the unclean spirit gone out.

familiar.text: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.

modern.text: And she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone. The Deaf and Mute Man (Matthew 9:27–34)

original.text: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσα εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς εὗρεν τὸ ⸂παιδίον βεβλημένον ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην καὶ τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐξεληλυθός⸃.

verses.restored: Again, going out from the borders of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, in the middle of the Decapolis borders.

familiar.text: And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.

modern.text: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.

original.text: Καὶ πάλιν ἐξελθὼν ἐκ τῶν ὁρίων Τύρου ⸂ἦλθεν διὰ Σιδῶνος εἰς⸃ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ὁρίων Δεκαπόλεως.

verses.restored: They brought to him a deaf man with difficulty speaking, and pleaded with him to place his hand on him.

familiar.text: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.

modern.text: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.

original.text: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ κωφὸν ⸀καὶ ⸀μογιλάλον, καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιθῇ αὐτῷ τὴν χεῖρα.

verses.restored: Taking him away from the crowd privately, he put his fingers into his ears, and after spitting touched his tongue.

familiar.text: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;

modern.text: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.

original.text: καὶ ἀπολαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου κατʼ ἰδίαν ἔβαλεν τοὺς δακτύλους αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ καὶ πτύσας ἥψατο τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: Looking up into heaven, he sighed deeply and said to him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

familiar.text: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

modern.text: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).

original.text: καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐστέναξεν, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εφφαθα, ὅ ἐστιν Διανοίχθητι·

verses.restored: His hearing was opened, the binding of his tongue was released, and he spoke plainly.

familiar.text: And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.

modern.text: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.

original.text: ⸀καὶ ⸀ἠνοίγησαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀκοαί, καὶ ἐλύθη ὁ δεσμὸς τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὀρθῶς·

verses.restored: Jesus ordered them to tell no one; but the more he ordered them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.

familiar.text: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it;

modern.text: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.

original.text: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ ⸀λέγωσιν· ὅσον δὲ ⸂αὐτοῖς διεστέλλετο, αὐτοὶ⸃ μᾶλλον περισσότερον ἐκήρυσσον.

verses.restored: They were exceedingly astonished, saying, He has done all things beautifully/well; he even makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak.

familiar.text: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.

modern.text: The people were utterly astonished and said, “He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”

original.text: καὶ ὑπερπερισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες· Καλῶς πάντα πεποίηκεν, καὶ τοὺς κωφοὺς ποιεῖ ἀκούειν ⸀καὶ ἀλάλους λαλεῖν.
